The issue was never reproduce on an official release by me or anyone who shared the feat with me, so it couldn't be addressed even if I believe it's a real issue (Saar has entered several high quality reports in the past and has deep experience with rmr2, so I am concerned about this). I need some user cooperation to be able to deal with any problem that I don't discover myself. If the user drops the ball while I haven't reproduced yet, there isn't much I can do.

> Is there a way to download the old "Latest Official RHadoop Release" - what was that 3.1.x?

The latest is 3.2.0 All past releases are tagged in git, so if you are comfortable with git just clone the project, list the tags with git tag, checkout the version of interest and build from source (package is under pkg dir). I'd rather fix 3.3.0 before we release it then send people backwards, but you know you priorities.

My first suspicion is an interaction with YARN containers and memory allocation. Since YARN, we found that container memory goes by default to java, and nothing is left for other processes, including R. So we added -- on top of my mind in 3.2.0 -- some hadoop configuration to address this, but the exact values were the result of an educated guess and regular testing.

These are the defaults

> rmr.options("backend.parameters")
$hadoop
$hadoop$D
[1] "mapreduce.map.java.opts=-Xmx400M"

$hadoop$D
[1] "mapreduce.reduce.java.opts=-Xmx400M"

$hadoop$D
[1] "mapreduce.map.memory.mb=4096"

$hadoop$D
[1] "mapreduce.reduce.memory.mb=4096"

You can change them with

rmr.options(backend.parameters = list(hadoop = list(property = value, ...)))

First thing I would try is to double the java space to 800M and see if that gets you through. I am not very confident about this because there is absolutely no reason for Java to need all that space in such a small example. When you set backend.parameters you'll get a deprecation message. Don't worry about it, I was hoping one day to be able to drop this abstraction loophole, but it doesn't seem to be happening and it's just a warning.

Another thing you could do is monitoring, and I am not sure how that would be done on your particular cluster, to try and see  how much memory java is actually using when it fails, and what else is using it up, if it's running out physically (unlikely) or running into poorly set limits.

I think we can call this a confirmed bug now, and we can always backtrack if it turns out to be some configuration problem. I opened an issue <https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/rmr2/issues/148> in the issue tracker and I would like to continue the discussion there as it's better set up for development. Thanks

It's more than a rumor that whirr will be soon moved to the attic. Its PMC said so <https://mail-archives.apache.org/mod_mbox/bigtop-dev/201409.mbox/%3CCAPbPdOZsbbwLi9YRNF2QBaTX=fCkhY9y=+Wz...@mail.gmail.com%3E>! It has also stopped working for us since CDH5. This is a problem for RHadoop. We really loved having a single way to test on multiple platforms via simple configuration changes. Does anyone deploy rmr2 to an EC2 cluster? How do you do it? Thanks!

Antonio

messages.body_plain:
Solved.
The solution is twofold.
1) Specify additional information to the mapreduce input.format
2) Redirect output to a directory, otherwise it fails in the reduce phase.

The final working program is:

#' First test on real data using RHadoop
#'
#' Simple test of text processing with rhadoop.
#'
run = function (inputdirectory = "/user/vcn_osd/input", outputdirectory = "/user/vcn_osd/output", vectorized.reducer = TRUE)
{
  mapper = function (key, line)
  {
    increment.counter ("Derrick", "lines", increment = nrow (line))
    keyval (as.numeric (line[[1]]), as.numeric (line[[11]]))
  }

  reducer = function (keys, values)
  {
    increment.counter ("Derrick", "values", increment = length (values))
    if (vectorized.reducer)
    {
      values = split (values, as.data.frame (keys), drop = TRUE)
      keyval (names (values), vsum (values))
    }
    else
      keyval (keys, sum (values))
  }

  out = mapreduce (
    input = inputdirectory,
    input.format = make.input.format (
      format = "csv", sep = ";", fileEncoding = "ISO8859-1", encoding = "ISO8859-1", stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
      col.names = c ("INTERNAL_LSB_ID", "INTERNAL_LSB_ID_2", "STATION_NAME", "YEAR", "MONTH", "DAY", "HOUR", "MINUTE", "SECOND", "SEASON", "VALUE", "UNIT", "QUALITY"),
      colClasses = c ("integer", "integer", "character", "integer", "integer", "integer", "integer", "integer", "integer", "character", "numeric", "character", "character")),
    output = outputdirectory,
    output.format = make.output.format (format = "csv"),
    map = mapper,
    combine = FALSE,
    reduce = reducer,
    vectorized.reduce = vectorized.reducer,
    verbose = TRUE
  )
}

messages.subject: some hadoop settings in rmr2
messages.subject_clean: some hadoop settings in rmr2
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
since users started switching to YARN we had reports of tasks running out of memory. The problem seems to be that containers have a certain amount of memory allocated to them and most of it gets used up by java and none is left for R. In 3.2.0 the mapreduce call tries to modify some hadoop settings so that the above is less likely to happen. The defaults are

> str(rmr.options("backend.parameters"))
List of 1
 $ hadoop:List of 4
  ..$ D: chr "mapreduce.map.java.opts=-Xmx400M"
  ..$ D: chr "mapreduce.reduce.java.opts=-Xmx400M"
  ..$ D: chr "mapreduce.map.memory.mb=4096"
  ..$ D: chr "mapreduce.reduce.memory.mb=4096"

While these worked on our test clusters, other types of failure ensued: java running out of heap space, container size exceeding max limits etc. We are about to release rmr 3.3.0 and, while there probably are no settings that will work across all deployments and applications, if we could get it to where it will work for most people until they are experienced enough to take charge and not to get discouraged, that would be progress. Our current view is to keep only the *.java.opts settings which should work unless the record size is large and go with the cluster defaults for the *memory.mb settings which are so hw dependent. Another possibility is to compel the user to set these parameters before launching jobs, rather then trying to run at guesstimated values and let people dig through the logs to figure out what went wrong.  I would love to hear from those of you who have made the switch to yarn and mr2, are these settings working and if not, how did you modify them? What would you like to see in 3.3.0? Thanks

In terms of "production" clusters, we have been working with Yarn for a while, but we're still using rmr 3.1.2. Unfortunately, we haven't had a chance to upgrade to 3.2 yet. The non-existing defaults of 3.1.2 worked fine, and when they didn't we found combinations that worked (for specific memory intensive jobs).

One problem I did run into is when installing rmr 3.2 on the HortonWorks Data Platform sandbox (2.1, haven't had a chance to try out 2.2 yet), which I use for teaching. The sandbox is a fully functional single node cluster that lives in a virtual machine, so memory there is very limited (4Gb RAM for the whole machine). When running code there, I include the following lines at the beginning of each script:

## hadoop specific definitions
rmr.options(backend.parameters = list(
  hadoop = list(D = "mapreduce.map.memory.mb=1024")
))

The HortonWorks sandbox is a very limited platform, for teaching / training purposes only, so I wouldn't take its limitations as a real guideline for usability... On the other hand, these sandboxes (both HortonWorks and Cloudera have ones) are sometimes people's first foray into the world of hadoop and R, so maybe the defaults should allow people to work with these very limited resources.

The extent to which I would 'compel' users to set these limits would be to have a warning in case the out-of-the-box defaults are used, similar to the "backend.parameters is deprecated" warning. As a novice user, I would prefer to do as little as possible.
